skills.name: Direct same-denominator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract fraction parts (and whole parts, if present) directly once denominators match and no borrowing is required.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find the LCD and convert fractions (or fraction parts of mixed numbers) with unlike denominators into equivalent fractions sharing a common denominator.

skills.name: Borrowing/regrouping
skills.definition: When the subtrahend's fraction part exceeds the minuend's, borrow one whole unit (as denominator/denominator) from the whole part and complete the subtraction.

skills.name: Whole number as mixed number
skills.definition: Rewrite a standalone whole-number operand as an equivalent mixed number with a zero-numerator fraction (n 0/d) so it can be processed like a mixed number.

skills.name: Simplify to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result that is not already in simplest form to its lowest-terms equivalent.

skills.name: Normalize improper fractional part
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fraction part's numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator into standard mixed-number form by carrying the excess into the whole part, before subtracting.

skills.name: Find LCD & convert
skills.definition: Determine the least common denominator for two fractions with different denominators and convert both to equivalent fractions with that denominator.

skills.name: Direct numerator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions (or fraction parts) that already share a common denominator, with no borrowing required, keeping the denominator.

skills.name: Simplify fraction
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction (intermediate or final result) to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.

skills.name: Separate whole/fraction parts
skills.definition: Split a mixed number (or treat a whole number as whole + 0/d) into whole-number and fractional components and subtract the whole-number parts independently.

skills.name: Borrow/regroup
skills.definition: When the fraction-part subtraction would be negative, borrow one whole unit (expressed as d/d) from the whole part, add it to the fraction part, and complete the subtraction.

skills.name: Normalize improper mixed fraction
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fractional part is improper (numerator ≥ denominator) into standard form by transferring the excess into the whole-number part before subtracting.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find the LCD of two unlike denominators and convert both fractions to equivalent fractions with that denominator.

skills.name: Same-denominator numerator subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions (or fractional parts) that already share a common denominator.

skills.name: Whole/fraction decomposition
skills.definition: Separate a mixed number (or whole number treated as whole + 0/d) into whole and fractional parts and subtract the whole parts independently.

skills.name: Borrowing/regrouping
skills.definition: When the fractional subtraction yields a negative value, borrow one unit from the whole (as d/d) and redo the fractional subtraction.

skills.name: Fraction simplification
skills.definition: Reduce a resulting fraction to lowest terms by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.

skills.name: Improper fraction-part normalization
skills.definition: Convert a mixed number whose fractional part is improper (numerator ≥ denominator) into standard proper mixed-number form before subtracting.

skills.name: Common Denominator Conversion
skills.definition: Find the LCD of two unlike denominators and convert both fractions into equivalent fractions with that denominator.

skills.name: Like-Fraction Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions that already share a common denominator to obtain the fractional part of the result.

skills.name: Whole-Number Subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the whole-number components of two mixed numbers or integers directly.

skills.name: Borrowing Across Whole and Fraction
skills.definition: When the fractional subtraction produces a negative value, borrow one whole unit (expressed as denominator/denominator), add it to the fraction, and re-subtract.

skills.name: Improper Fractional-Part Normalization
skills.definition: Recognize that the fractional part of a mixed number is improper (numerator ≥ denominator) and convert it into a proper mixed number before subtracting.

skills.name: Fraction Simplification
skills.definition: Reduce the resulting fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common divisor to express the answer in lowest terms.

skills.name: Common denominator conversion
skills.definition: Find the LCD of two unlike denominators and rewrite both fractions as equivalent fractions over that denominator.

skills.name: Pure fraction subtraction
skills.definition: Subtract the numerators of two fractions sharing a common denominator when neither operand has a whole-number part.

skills.name: Whole/fraction part separation
skills.definition: Split mixed numbers (or whole numbers treated as whole+0/d) into whole and fractional parts and subtract each part independently.

skills.name: Borrowing/regrouping
skills.definition: When the fractional subtraction yields a negative value, convert one whole unit into denominator/denominator and add it to the fraction part before subtracting again.

skills.name: Normalize improper fractional part
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number whose fractional part is improper (numerator ≥ denominator) into standard form by extracting whole units before subtracting.

skills.name: Simplify to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fractional result by dividing numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor.
